title: Invite quarantine + domain proofing with RBACv2 assertions and audit hooks for partner onboarding
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Partner and cross-tenant onboarding currently allows org admins to invite external users after a simple email check. We lack a quarantine workflow for invites that fail domain proofing or match denylist heuristics, plus RBAC v2 needs to record assertion context (who elevated invite, SAML group origin, allowed admin scope). Without audit hooks and assertion metadata we cannot reliably rollback or automate remediation for suspicious invites.

Goal: Implement an invite quarantine flow that: 1) performs domain proofing (DNS TXT or HTTPS token) for invited external domains when the org permit_mode != 'open'; 2) marks invites that fail checks as QUARANTINED instead of DELIVERED; 3) attaches RBAC v2 assertion metadata (inviter_role, inviter_scope, sso_group_hash) to each invite event; and 4) emits structured audit logs for quarantine, approval, and auto-revocation actions. Additionally add an admin console workflow to review and approve quarantined invites tied to a fast-track path for verified partners (partner_allowlist).
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine state exists for invites (PENDING -> QUARANTINED -> APPROVED/REJECTED) and is visible in org audit logs
Domain proofing runs for any invite where invite.domain != org.verified_domains and org.invite_policy != 'open'
RBAC v2 assertion metadata is persisted with every invite event (inviter_id, inviter_role_key, sso_group_hash, claim_source)
Audit logs (structured JSON) include invite_id, quarantine_reason, proofing_result, assertion_metadata, and actor metadata and are forwarded to our audit pipeline
Console has a 'Quarantine review' table with filters (domain, risk_score, invited_at) and actions to Approve / Reject / Escalate
Automated tests cover domain proofing success/fail, quarantine transition state machine, and audit record emission
Feature gated behind feature-flag: invite_quarantine_rbac_v2 for gradual rollout to 20% of orgs initially
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature-flag for internal orgs and 5 selected partner customers; monitor audit logs for false positives for 7 days. Phase 2: open to 20% of orgs with telemetry thresholds; enable console review. Phase 3: global on by default with partner_allowlist import tools. Toggle to disable via invite_quarantine_rbac_v2 FF.
test_plan: Unit: domain proofing module returns PASS/FAIL/UNCONFIRMED for DNS and HTTPS methods
Integration: invite API returns 202 with state QUARANTINED when domain proofing fails
E2E: console reviewer approves quarantined invite which transitions to APPROVED and triggers email send
Audit: verify structured audit messages arrive in Kafka topic 'audit.invites' and contain assertion_metadata
Security: run fuzzing on invite payloads and confirm RBAC v2 assertion validation prevents privilege escalation
implementation_notes: Add InviteState enum value QUARANTINED and state machine transitions in identity-service (see ENG-299002 for state infra)
Domain proofing: implement DNS TXT check + HTTPS token endpoint. Prefer async proofing with callback to avoid blocking UX (store proofing_job_id)
RBAC v2: extend Assertion proto to include inviter_role_key and sso_group_hash; require propagation through gateway and identity-service
Audit: emit structured event 'invite.quarantine' and 'invite.decision' to audit pipeline; include correlation_id for traceability
Console: add review endpoint /orgs/{id}/quarantined-invites with pagination and bulk actions
Performance: proofing should be rate-limited per org and batched where possible to avoid DNS/HTTP hot loops
Privacy: store only hashed SSO group identifier (sso_group_hash) and strip raw group names from logs to meet minimization policy
